full_judgment: 29. So far the other appeal being Second Appeal No. 307 of 1976 arising out of the suit of the appellant being Title Suit No. 221 of 1973 for declaration of title and recovery of possession in the suit-land, it appears that the trial Court decreed the suit in part, but the lower appellate Court totally dismissed the same on a misconception of law and facts. Admittedly, the plaintiff of the above suit was the owner of the suit-land but he was out of possession of the same after entering into the contract for sale of the same to defendant-respondent Nuruddin Ansari. Thus it appears that ownership of Santosh Kumar Paul in the suit land was not disputed and his suit was rightly decreed in part by the trial Court but wrongly dismissed by the lower appellate Court. Hence, I hold that this second Appeal of the appellant should be allowed in part so far his title in the suit-land was concerned but his prayer for recovery of khas possession should be dismissed. He may however he allowed to recover his possession in the suit land subject to payment of the entire amount of solacium as stated above along with the earnest money of Taka 901.00 to Nuruddin Ansari, the defendant of this suit within the period as fixed above.
